'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Middle Eastern crisis (2023–present)|Middle Eastern crisis]]
**[[Gaza war]]
***[[Mass detentions in the Gaza war]]
****[[Palestine|Palestinian]] media reports that [[Israel]] has released 60 [[Gazans|Gazan]] detainees back to the [[Gaza Strip]]. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog_entry/israel-releases-60-gazan-detainees-nabbed-during-the-war/ (''The Times of Israel'')]
***The [[Israel Defense Forces]] (IDF) and [[Shin Bet]] state that [[Hamas]]' internal security head Wael Musa Khaled Ladawi was killed in a [[airstrike]] in the [[Deir al-Balah]] area of the central [[Gaza Strip]], in violation of the ongoing ceasefire. [https://www.thejc.com/news/israel/israeli-airstrike-kills-hamas-internal-security-chief-in-central-gaza-lfur1eow (''The Jewish Chronicle'')]
***The IDF claim that [[Palestinian Islamic Jihad]] [[Nukhba forces|Nukhba]] militant Amro Abu Alrish and [[Hamas]] commander Abd Al-Nasser Al-Aziz Maqadmeh were killed in separate strikes in Gaza, which violated the ongoing ceasefire. [https://www.jpost.com/israel-news/defense-news/article-903806 (''The Jerusalem Post'')]
**[[2026 Iran war]]
***[[2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations]]
****[[Iran]] and the [[United States]] pause [[July 2026 United States strikes against Iran|strikes]] as the U.S. allows additional time for negotiations and Iran suspends retaliatory attacks against U.S. allies. [https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/07/28/world/americas-emea/us-iran-pause-strikes-to-give-talks-some-space/2392066 (AFP via ''The Manila Times'')]
***[[Saudi Arabia in the 2026 Iran war]]
****[[Saudi Arabia]]'s [[Ministry of Defense (Saudi Arabia)|defense ministry]] reports intercepting drones fired by Iran-backed [[Islamic Resistance in Iraq|Iraqi militias]] from inside [[Iraq]], which targeted [[Petroleum industry in Saudi Arabia|oil facilities]] in [[Eastern Province (Saudi Arabia)|eastern Saudi Arabia]] and the [[Riyadh]] area. [https://www.france24.com/en/middle-east/20260727-saudi-arabia-says-it-intercepted-drones-from-iraq-as-houthis-target-oil-sites (France 24)]
**[[Yemeni civil war (2014–present)|Yemeni civil war]]
***[[Houthi–Saudi Arabian conflict]], [[Saudi-led intervention in the Yemeni civil war]]
****The [[Houthis]] launch a [[Drone warfare|drone attack]] that damages the [[Abqaiq oil field]] in eastern Saudi Arabia. [https://www.bbc.com/persian/live/c4gx4v6ex0dt (BBC Persian)] [https://www.france24.com/en/middle-east/20260727-saudi-arabia-says-it-intercepted-drones-from-iraq-as-houthis-target-oil-sites (France 24)]
*[[Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|Sudanese civil war]]
**[[Kordofan campaign (2023–present)|Kordofan campaign]]
***[[Siege of El Obeid]]
****Drone strikes are reported in [[El-Obeid]], [[North Kordofan]], [[Sudan]], hours after the [[Sudanese Armed Forces]] (SAF) secured the National Export Highway, which connects Sudan's capital [[Khartoum]] and North Kordofan. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260727-drone-strikes-rock-sudan-s-el-obeid-after-army-secures-highway (AFP via France 24)] [https://thedefensepost.com/2026/07/27/sudan-el-obeid-drone-strikes/ (''The Defense Post'')]
***The Sudanese Doctors Network reports that the main hospital in [[Jebrat al Sheikh District]], North Kordofan, has been looted and turned into a military barracks. [https://sudantribune.com/article/316666 (''Sudan Tribune'')]
***SAF [[general]] and leader [[Abdel Fattah al-Burhan]] visits the newly captured areas in North Kordofan alongside [[Sudan Shield Forces]] leader [[Abu Aqla Kaikal]] and [[Darfur]] [[Darfur Regional Government|Governor]] [[Minni Minnawi|Minni Arko Minnawi]]. [https://sudantribune.com/article/316686 (''Sudan Tribune'')]
**The Sudanese ''National Mine Action Center'' (NMAC) reports that 80% of war remnants have been removed from the [[Khartoum State]] and announces plans to expand survey and removal operations in [[Sudan|Sudanese]] areas recently recaptured by the SAF. [https://sudantribune.net/article/316687 (''Sudan Tribune'' <small>in Arabic</small>)]
'''Arts and culture'''
*[[UNESCO]] designates the [[Amazon Theatre]] and [[Theatro da Paz]], [[opera house]]s in the [[Amazonia]] region of [[Brazil]], as [[World Heritage Site]]s. [https://apnews.com/article/brazil-amazon-theaters-unesco-world-heritage-belem-manaus-bc9224cd6e60481265dfea49a2de46e8 (AP)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Canada–United States relations]]
**[[2025–2026 United States trade war with Canada and Mexico]]
***The [[Gordie Howe International Bridge]], which [[Detroit–Windsor|connects]] between [[Detroit]], [[Michigan]], U.S., and [[Windsor, Ontario]], [[Canada]], officially opens to traffic after months of delay due to the countries' [[trade war]] and the [[Tariffs in the second Trump administration|U.S. imposition of tariffs]] on Canada. [https://www.freep.com/story/news/local/michigan/detroit/2026/07/27/gordie-howe-bridge-opening-toll/91035549007/ (''Detroit Free Press'')] [https://globalnews.ca/news/11994915/gordie-howe-bridge-open/ (Global News)]
*[[Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war]]
**[[Singapore]]'s [[Monetary Authority of Singapore|monetary authority]] tightens its [[monetary policy]] for the second time in three months by increasing the [[Singapore dollar]]'s [[Currency appreciation and depreciation|appreciation]] rate against a trade-weighted [[currency basket]], citing rising [[Economy of Singapore|import]] costs and [[inflation]] risks caused by the Iran war. [https://www.scmp.com/news/asia/southeast-asia/article/3361951/singapore-tightens-monetary-policy-second-time-3-months (AFP via ''South China Morning Post'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[Wildfires in 2026]]
**[[2026 France wildfires]]
***Wildfires continue in the [[Gironde]] region near [[Bordeaux]], [[France]], as [[President of France|president]] [[Emmanuel Macron]] describes it as "the worst fire-related crisis since [[France during World War II|World War II]]." [https://apnews.com/article/europe-wildfires-france-spain-bordeaux-01d41aae7a3c835b270306288023f8e3 (AP)]
*[[2026 Pacific hurricane season]]
**Hurricane Genevieve strengthens into a [[List of Category 5 Pacific hurricanes|category 5 pacific hurricane]], the first in the Pacific region since [[2024 Pacific hurricane season|2024]]. [https://www.the-independent.com/news/world/americas/major-hurricane-genevieve-east-pacific-mexico-b3022360.html (''The Independent'')]
*The death toll from heavy rains and flooding in [[Pakistan]] since June increases to 107 people killed and at least 344 others injured. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/7/27/death-toll-from-pakistan-monsoon-rains-floods-tops-100 (Al Jazeera)]
*A [[landslide]] occurs at the [[Gold Ridge Mine]] in [[Guadalcanal]], [[Solomon Islands]]. Local media reports ten bodies recovered, while the [[Ministry of Health and Medical Services (Solomon Islands)|National Referral Hospital]] says it expects more fatalities. [https://www.bssnews.net/international/409227 (AFP via BSS)]

**The General Coordination for Refugees and Displaced Persons in [[Darfur]], [[Sudan]], reports seven [[cholera]] cases across the region in displacement camps between July 5 and July 25. [https://sudantribune.com/article/316707 (''Sudan Tribune'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[Brazil–Lithuania relations]]
**The [[Lithuania]]n [[Government of Lithuania|government]] registers a resolution to open [[List of diplomatic missions of Lithuania|an embassy]] in [[Brasilia]], Brazil, in October. The country currently has a [[consul (diplomacy)|consulate-general]] in [[São Paulo]]. [https://www.lrt.lt/en/news-in-english/19/3003229/lithuania-plans-opening-embassy-in-brazil (LRT)]
*[[Kuwait–Pakistan relations]]
**[[Kuwait]] approves the [[Kuwait–Pakistan Defence Cooperation Agreement]], a five-year framework for defence cooperation between the two countries covering military training, exchanges, defence technology, logistics, and cooperation between their armed forces. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/middle-east/kuwait-ratifies-defense-cooperation-agreement-with-pakistan/4010217 (Anadolu Ajansı)] [https://www.jordannews.jo/Section-20/Middle-East/Kuwait-Approves-Defense-Cooperation-Agreement-with-Pakistan-53493 (Jordan News)]
*[[Romania–Russia relations]], [[Violations of non-combatant airspace during the Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Violations of non-combatant airspace during the Russo-Ukrainian war]]
**[[Romania]] recalls its ambassador to [[Russia]], declares a [[Russian embassy]] employee ''[[persona non grata]]'', and summons [[List of ambassadors of Russia to Romania|Russia's ambassador]] after three [[Unmanned Systems Forces of Russia|Russian drones]] violated Romanian [[airspace]] between July 24 and 26. [https://english.news.cn/20260727/198c7415c42d486299afc60244b97cf6/c.html (Xinhua)]
*[[Chad]] states its intention to [[States parties to the Rome Statute#Withdrawal|withdraw]] from the [[International Criminal Court]], citing limited effectiveness and disproportionate attention to [[Africa]]n cases. If upheld, the ruling may void his victory and require Yoon's [[People Power Party]] to repay [[campaign fund]]s.
